transcript: Lou Wall is a master in never letting them know your next move. In her solo show Breaking The Fifth Wall at Soho Playhouse, she explores artifice and the role of lies in performance. This comes with some elaborately constructed bits that blur truth and reality, and by the end, your brain may be melting. I think the coolest part about this is how the sequencing of topics often feels haphazard, but ends up being the perfect breeding ground for some really satisfying callbacks. It's confusing by design along the way, but I found the individual bits to be entertaining enough in their own right that I could just take in the roughly 60-minute ride as it came. Lou touches on her viral Facebook Marketplace debacle, Betterhelp, therapy and even true crime. Part comedy, but very much part theater in how much it leans into playing pretend, this piece is deeply original and a charmingly meta examination of storytelling itself. Breaking The Fifth Wall is running at Soho Playhouse through this weekend.
